records.name: Varvara
records.facts_used: Varvara: The documented comparison leads to the Barbara family. Greek barbaros described a foreigner or speaker of another language; in the feminine name it is commonly rendered foreign woman. This ancient word history does not judge a modern bearer’s identity or character. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Varvara: eighteenth century. Its calendar year is 1937. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš exact Varvara→Barbara via Slavic forms, own eighteenth-century use/calendar1937. No invented exact year.

records.name: Osmundas
records.facts_used: Osmundas: Lithuanian Osmundas belongs to the Osmund family. Old English ōs and Old Norse áss/óss mean god, while mund/mundr denotes a protector. These historical stems can be explained separately; their meanings do not predict a bearer’s abilities. The Dictionary of Medieval Names records Latin Osmundus in England in 1189, citing a documentary edition. This is a concrete example of the family’s written transmission. The date belongs to the related Latin form, not the first registration of Lithuanian Osmundas.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: DMNES Latin1189 nominativeOsmundus GASurvp82, not genitive1183. No date transfer to Lithuanian form.
